first_lines: Supplemental video. Fluoroscopic assessment of diaphragmatic motion and ventilation during PFA in Case 3
Sequential fluoroscopic clips demonstrate changes in diaphragmatic motion and ventilation during LIPV PFA:
Before PFA: Normal diaphragmatic excursion is observed during mechanical ventilation.
During initial PFA: Coughing is induced, resulting in sustained diaphragmatic elevation.
Post-PFA delivery: Diaphragmatic motion is minimal due to impaired mechanical ventilation.
Two minutes post-PFA: Manual ventilation gradually restores airflow, and diaphragmatic motion reappears.
Three minutes post-PFA: Ventilation and diaphragmatic motion return to baseline.
LIPV, left inferior pulmonary vein; PFA, pulsed field ablation.
